R0272.title: Embodied Agent Jailbreak & Over-Autonomy Risk
R0272.definition: The risk that an embodied agent, jailbreak-induced or due to over-broad autonomy permissions, invokes physical tools or performs physical actions beyond intended boundaries, causing irreversible physical-world consequences.
R0272.description:
Embodied agent jailbreak & over-autonomy risk is the physical-world amplification of model-layer attacks. A RoboPAIR-jailbroken Unitree Go2 can be induced to perform harmful physical actions such as finding weapons, striking pedestrians, and ignoring stop signs. Unlike pure software agents, an embodied agent's post-jailbreak misoperation translates directly into irreversible physical-world consequences — software-agent misoperations can be rolled back, but embodied-agent actions like opening doors, transporting items, or manipulating robotic arms cannot be undone. Over-autonomy risk refers to the agent being granted over-broad action permissions, overly loose goals, or ambiguous task boundaries and then performing physical actions in unintended situations; this differs from maliciously induced jailbreak.

A safe high-level task does not guarantee safe decomposed subtasks. When an attacker or ordinary user gives an instruction such as "clean the kitchen" or "handle this" without a clear object, action, or scope, the planner may expand the task and produce hazardous steps such as handling knives, opening cabinets, moving glassware, or approaching children. If the system reviews only high-level intent or grants the planning model direct authority over skills and motors, semantic ambiguity and inherited context errors become physical-action boundary violations. This risk relates to R0148 (AI agent tool abuse / over-autonomy risk), but R0148 focuses on general AI agents while this risk is specialized for physical-action overstep of embodied agents, emphasizing physical irreversibility.
R0272.influence: A jailbroken agent can manipulate robotic arms, open doors, transport items, or strike people; autonomous decision errors translate directly into physical harm, unlike the controllable rollback of pure software agents — consequences are irreversible and may cause casualties.
